Postdoc in Solid-State Batteries – Scalable Production of Solid Electrolytes
Login and apply
KTH Royal Institute of Technology, School of Engineering Sciences in Chemistry, Biotechnology and Health
Job description
Next leap in the battery development is expected to be the lithium solid-state batteries (SSB), allowing the replacement of the flammable organic electrolyte in Li-ion batteries with a safer and a more compact solid electrolyte. Within the framework of the Swedish governmental battery initiative COMPEL, aimed to support competence and excellence in battery research and education for the transport sector, KTH join forces with a coordinated initiative on composite SSB with seven postdoctoral positions in several disciplines, focusing on various aspects along the battery value chain, ranging from synthesis, cell assembly, characterization, modeling to scaled-up manufacturing. The 2-year postdoc project
Scalable Production of Ceramic Solid Electrolytes for Solid-State Batteries
will be carried out jointly at the Div. Process technology and Resource Recovery at the Dept. Chemical Engineering. This project, grounded in chemical engineering, will focus on the development of scalable solvent mediated processes for production of sulfide or halide electrolytes. Particular emphasis will be placed on obtaining particles with controlled size distribution and morphology that enable good and reproducible electrolyte performance. In parallel, industrial aspects such as solvent recovery, solid-liquid separation, drying, and process intensification will be addressed. The goal is to gain a better fundamental understanding of the processes involved and to generate scalable process concepts to support the industrial manufacturing of next-generation solid-state battery electrolytes.
Qualifications
Requirements
A doctoral degree or an equivalent foreign degree in Chemical Engineering, Materials Science, or a related subject. This eligibility requirement must be met no later than the time the employment decision is made.
Proficiency in written and spoken English
,
as this will be required in day-to-day work.
Strong laboratory and instrumental skills.
Awareness of diversity and equal treatment issues with a particular focus on gender equality.
Preferred qualifications
A doctoral degree or an equivalent foreign degree, obtained within the last three years prior to the application deadline.
Experience in solid-state batteries and material synthesis.
An innovative mindset and ability to work independently.
Good collaborative skills and abilities and interest in working in a team.
Great emphasis will be placed on personal skills.

Log into KTH's recruitment system to apply for this position. You are responsible for ensuring that your application is complete according to the instructions in the ad.
The application must include:

Copy of diplomas and grades from your university studies. Translations into English or Swedish if the original documents have not been issued in any West-European languages.
Brief account of why you want to conduct research, your academic interests and how they relate to your previous studies and future goals. Maximally one page long.

Your complete application must be received at KTH no later than the last day of application, midnight CET/CEST (Central European Time/Central European Summer Time).

ai.summary: 2-year postdoctoral position in scalable production of ceramic solid electrolytes for solid-state batteries at KTH's Department of Chemical Engineering. Research develops solvent-mediated processes for synthesis of sulfide and halide electrolytes, focusing on particle morphology control, solvent recovery, and process intensification.

thematic_fit.rationale: Position is chemical engineering and materials synthesis. No human-centred design, no immersive systems, no learning or collaboration research, no spatial cognition. This is pure materials manufacturing process development—categorically orthogonal to HCI.

methodological_fit.rationale: Research methodology is experimental materials synthesis, process chemistry, and engineering design of production systems. No overlap with human-centred empirical methods (user studies, UX evaluation, collaborative system design).

growth_value.rationale: No growth toward target identity. No capability in spatial understanding, immersive learning, collaboration frameworks, or human factors would be developed. This is a complete disciplinary detour.

strategic_value.rationale: KTH is a leading institution and Stockholm is preferred. However, the position is embedded in chemical engineering and process technology, not HCI or immersive systems research. No network or supervisor alignment with target identity.

eligibility_flags: Requires doctoral degree by employment decision; researcher has MSc by Research in progress—contingent on thesis conferment.
Position requires 'strong laboratory and instrumental skills' and 'experience in solid-state batteries and material synthesis'—researcher has neither.
risks: Pure chemical engineering and materials science—entirely outside HCI and immersive systems research.
No human factors, no user interaction, no learning science, no collaboration research.
Acceptance would represent a fundamental pivot away from stated target identity and would be professionally isolating within HCI networks.
